title: Rings and Rods
summary: Given a string rings of length 2n that describes n rings, where each ring is either red ('R'), green ('G'), or blue ('B'), and is placed on one of ten rods labeled from '0' to '9', count the number of rods that have at least one ring of each color ('R', 'G', 'B').
statement: Given a string rings of length 2n that describes n rings, where each ring is either red ('R'), green ('G'), or blue ('B'), and is placed on one of ten rods labeled from '0' to '9', count the number of rods that have at least one ring of each color ('R', 'G', 'B').
constraints: rings consists of color-digit pairs; colors are R, G, or B and rods are zero through nine.
Multiple rings of the same color on one rod count only once.
Return the number of rods carrying all three colors.
hints: A three-bit mask records which colors have appeared on each rod.
Assign one bit to R, G, and B and OR it into the indexed rod mask.
After all pairs, count masks equal to binary 111.
OR is idempotent for duplicate colors, and mask seven occurs exactly when every color bit is present.
editorial: OR is idempotent for duplicate colors, and mask seven occurs exactly when every color bit is present.

tests.explanation: Only rod zero has red, green, and blue rings.
Rod zero still counts once despite repeated colors.
